questions.question: What distinguishes an operational governance platform from a policy document?
options: It connects rules and evidence to release, runtime restriction, and accountable decisions
It publishes a longer list of principles
It produces one ethics score for every use case
It removes the need for human judgment
questions.explanation: Governance is operational when it can change whether and how a specific version ships or runs, with evidence and accountable authority attached.

questions.question: Why should governance classify the use case rather than the model family alone?
options: Model architecture completely determines legal obligations
The same model can create very different consequences under different purposes, authority, data, and affected populations
Use cases never change after release
Only model size determines risk
questions.explanation: Risk emerges from the system in context: its intended use, workflow, authority, data, scale, reversibility, and effect on people.

questions.question: A threshold change leaves the model artifact untouched. Why can it still require re-evaluation?
options: Thresholds change the balance of positive and negative outcomes and may change subgroup error rates
Thresholds only change UI colors
An unchanged artifact guarantees unchanged impact
Thresholds eliminate the need for monitoring
questions.explanation: The operating threshold is part of the decision system. Moving it changes who is selected, missed, or incorrectly flagged.

questions.question: Which release record provides the strongest evidence that the deployed model was actually reviewed?
options: A mutable folder named approved
A meeting note without an artifact identifier
Versioned evidence and approval bound to the deployed artifact digest
A generic fairness policy
questions.explanation: Binding evidence to an immutable digest prevents approval for one artifact from silently authorizing another.

questions.question: A model has equal aggregate accuracy but a much higher false-negative rate for one affected group. What should governance do?
options: Publish only aggregate accuracy
Investigate the relevant harm, uncertainty, subgroup data, acceptance criterion, and mitigation
Assume demographic parity will solve every problem
Remove subgroup monitoring
questions.explanation: Aggregate metrics can hide concentrated harm. The relevant error, sample quality, uncertainty, cause, and response all require review.

questions.question: When is human oversight an effective control?
options: Whenever a person is shown the model output
Only when the person has context, time, competence, authority, and a tested path to override or escalate
When overrides are technically impossible
When the automated outcome occurs before review
questions.explanation: A nominal reviewer cannot mitigate harm. Effective oversight requires usable information, sufficient capacity, and real authority before the consequence becomes irreversible.
